resources.string: Made on this phone while you watch. Speech recognition and translation run offline, and the app has no internet access, so your movies never leave the device.
No movies yet. Open a video to get English subtitles for it.
%1$s is removed from the list and its subtitles are deleted, so they would be made again next time. The video file itself is not touched.
Removed from the list. Its subtitles are kept for next time.
Pick the file once more so the app may read it.
Nothing to download: every model is part of the app and works offline. This phone has %1$s GB of memory, so the app uses %2$s unless you choose another speech model in Settings.
How far ahead subtitles must be ready before playback starts. Use High Accuracy or Full Movie if your phone is slower than real time.
Bigger models are more accurate but slower. Automatic picks the best one for this phone\'s memory.
Automatic uses M2M100 with Whisper tiny and base, where it translates much better, and Whisper\'s own translation with small, which scored a little higher in tests and is faster.
This phone is 32-bit, so Whisper translates (M2M100 needs a 64-bit phone).
Automatic detection works for most films; pick the language if it is misdetected (for example Bengali).
Use only the fast CPU cores (%1$d of %2$d)
Keeps recognition off the slow power-saving cores, which would otherwise hold the fast ones back.
All cores of this phone run at the same speed, so no core is left out.

Half the threads, faster translation settings and no background work beyond the look-ahead. This also turns on by itself when the system Power Saver is on, the battery is at 15 % or less and not charging, or the phone is hot.
Pause playback while subtitles are not ready
Keep translating the whole movie in the background
Open movies in landscape full screen
Widescreen videos turn to landscape and fill the screen. The full-screen button in the player switches back to portrait.
Audio track for playback and subtitles

Everything runs on this device: audio is decoded from your video, recognised by Whisper (whisper.cpp) and translated to English, and the results are cached so a movie is never processed twice. Live Floating Subtitles treat the sound they hear the same way, in memory only. The app has no internet permission, so nothing is uploaded or downloaded.
whisper.cpp and CTranslate2 run on the phone\'s processor, using its %1$s instructions.
whisper.cpp and CTranslate2 run on the phone\'s processor.

AC-3, E-AC-3, DTS and TrueHD through FFmpeg %1$s, used only when the phone has no decoder of its own. These libraries are replaceable, and their source code is included in the app; see the FFmpeg section of the notices.
Not included in this build, so AC-3 and DTS play only if the phone decodes them.
Only %1$.0f%% of the movie has subtitles so far. Export what is ready?
Watch foreign-language videos in other apps with automatically translated English subtitles.

Listens to the sound of the app playing the video, through Android\'s playback capture. Only apps that allow it can be heard: many streaming apps block it, and protected (DRM) videos are never captured. The app tells you when that happens.

Listens through the microphone, with subtitles floating over the video. Best when the video plays on a speaker, TV or laptop near the phone. From this phone\'s own speaker it works less well: the sound reaches the microphone weaker and with room echo, and some phones restrict the microphone.
The phone listens to a TV, laptop or another phone and shows large subtitles on its own screen. No overlay is needed.

Fast shows a provisional line while it is spoken and ends lines on short pauses. High Accuracy waits for longer pauses, gives the model more context and decodes more carefully, so lines come later but break less.
Look, timing, audio and performance of live subtitles
Blocked: the playing app does not allow its sound to be captured
. Falling behind: some lines were skipped. Try Fast quality or a smaller speech model.
Whisper\'s own translation, on this phone
Not used: subtitles show in this app
Offline: recognition and translation run on this phone, nothing is sent anywhere
%1$.1f s on average over the last %7$d lines (pause %2$d ms, waiting %3$d ms, recognition %4$d ms, translation %5$d ms, display %6$d ms)
Duration %1$s · speech recognised %2$.1f min · %3$d lines, %4$d translated by M2M100 · average latency %5$.1f s · %6$d lines skipped as too late. Processing cost: none, everything ran on this phone.

Audio is processed in memory on this phone and never saved or sent. Dialogue context is kept only while a session runs and is deleted when it stops. A notification and the floating button show whenever audio is being processed; Stop ends it at once.

The app will listen to the sound of videos playing on this phone to make English subtitles. Android asks for two things: permission to record audio (Android uses this name for capturing other apps\' sound too; the microphone is not used) and a screen-sharing confirmation. Only sound is captured, never the picture. Everything stays on this phone and nothing is saved.
The app will listen through the microphone to make English subtitles while you watch. Audio is processed in memory on this phone and never saved or sent. A notification shows while it listens.
The app will listen through the microphone to the TV or device playing the video and show large English subtitles on this phone. Audio is processed in memory on this phone and never saved or sent.
To show subtitles over YouTube and other apps, Android needs the \"Display over other apps\" permission. On the next screen, turn it on for AI Subtitle Translator, then come back.
Floating subtitles need \"Display over other apps\". Without it, use External device mode, which shows the subtitles in this app.
Live subtitles need permission to record audio, also for internal audio. You can allow it in the app\'s settings under Permissions.
Internal audio needs Android 10 or later. Use the microphone instead.
The screen-sharing confirmation could not be used. Start again.
Internal audio needs the screen-sharing confirmation (only sound is captured). You can use the microphone instead.
Android did not let live subtitles run in the background. Open the app and start again.

The video app is playing, but Android delivers only silence: this app does not allow its sound to be captured (many streaming apps and all protected videos do this). The app does not get around that. You can switch to the microphone; the phone then listens to the speaker or a TV nearby.
This app does not allow its sound to be captured.
This app blocks sound capture. You can listen through the microphone instead.
Screen sharing was stopped, so live subtitles ended.
Stopped after %1$d minutes without speech, to save battery.
Listen through the microphone instead? It picks up this phone\'s speaker or a TV nearby. Nothing is recorded or saved.
%1$.1f s · pause %2$d · wait %3$d · speech %4$d · translate %5$d · draw %6$d ms
Shown while live subtitles listen, with Pause and Stop.
Listening to the sound of the playing app, on this phone only
Listening through the microphone, on this phone only
Listening to another device through the microphone
Long lines wrap automatically and are shown in parts.
Automatic uses the base model where memory allows (tiny on small phones), because live subtitles need speed. Small is more accurate but on most phones too slow to keep up.
The last few lines guide the next one, which keeps names and wording consistent. Kept only during the session; nothing is saved.

Lines appear this long after the words were spoken, if they are ready by then. A line can never appear before it has been recognised, so values below the measured latency only make lines appear as soon as they are ready.
Android\'s noise suppressor on the microphone.
This phone has no noise suppressor for apps.
Raise it when the TV is far away or quiet.
Saves battery if you forget to stop it.
Threads, fast cores and battery saver
Shared with the movie player: open Settings
None: the app has no internet permission
Average delay from the end of speech to the subtitle, split into its stages.
Whisper reads only the length of each line instead of a full 30 seconds. Much faster; turn off if lines come out cut short.
